chunks: The holders of the book will throw it away, and its memorizers will forget it.
The Book and its people on that day will be exiled and expelled, two companions keeping together on one path, but no one will offer them asylum.
Consequently, at that time the Book and its people will be among the people but not among them, will be with them but not with them.
Because misguidance cannot accord with guidance, even though they may be together.
The people will have united on division, and will therefore have cut away from the community.
As though they were the leaders of the Book and not the Book their leader.
Nothing of it will be left with them except its name, and they will know nothing save its writing and its words.
Before that, they will inflict hardships on the virtuous, naming the latter’s truthful views about Allah false allegations, and enforcing for virtues the punishment of the vice.

key_terms.أَهْلُهُ: Its people (those who adhere to the Quran)

ai.seo_question: How does Nahj al-Balagha describe the relationship between the Quran and its people during times of spiritual decline?
ai.summary: Imam Ali describes a state of profound spiritual alienation where the Quran and its true adherents become 'exiled' among the people, retained only in name and script while its guidance is lost. This reflects the Shia scholarly concept of *al-Ghaybah al-Sughra* or general decline, where the community clings to the form of revelation but loses its essence, leading to a divergence between the text and its interpreters. The passage underscores the consequence of prioritizing superficial adherence over substantive practice, resulting in a fractured community that is physically present but spiritually absent.

en.sayed-ali-raza: The holders of the book will throw it away and its memorizers would forget it.
In these days the Qur’ān and its people will be exiled and expelled. They will be companions keeping together on one path, but no one will offer them asylum.
Consequently at this time the Qur’ān and its people will be among the people but not among them, will be with them but not with them,
because misguidance cannot accord with guidance even though they may be together.
The people will have united on division and will therefore have cut away from the community,
as though they were the leaders of the Qur’ān and not the Qur’ān their leader.
Nothing of it will be left with them except its name, and they will know nothing save its writing and its words.
Before that, they will inflict hardships on the virtuous, naming the latter’s truthful views about Allāh false allegations, and enforcing for virtues the punishment of the vice.
